Do states accurately determine eligibility and benefits?

The USDA defines payment error rates as measuring "the accuracy of each state’s eligibility and benefit determinations." This is not a measure of fraud.

If eligibility or benefit determinations are incorrect, the state may pay too much, termed an over payment, or too little, an under payment, in SNAP benefits to the receiving household. The USDA reports the rates of over and under payments as a percent of all state cases, and as a weighted national average.

Note that there is a error threshold that allows for small miscalculations; in 2025, this amount is $57.

As far as I can tell from this Anchorage Daily News article, this error rate does not include cases where a person is denied entirely incorrectly, and later deemed to have been eligible.

The USDA charges a penalty to states which have high payment error rates for two consecutive years (higher than the national payment error rate) and "meet additional statuatory criteria".
